**Sua missão:** preparar e executar uma comparação real entre o caminho atual do Hermes e o fast path System 1, usando mensagens humanas verdadeiras, BrowserTask nativa, snapshots independentes e recibos verificáveis.

Quando estiver pronto, responda **PRONTO PARA FRASE EXATA** e informe quais variantes estão efetivamente disponíveis. Vou enviar a frase de localização como uma nova mensagem, isoladamente.

Depois, valide a referência selecionada por snapshot fresco, confirme o recibo, a identidade da tarefa e o provedor utilizado. Meça latência e chamadas reais ao System 2 quando houver instrumentação confiável. Teste também os cenários de correspondência parcial, duplicidade e ausência de alvo.

Não invente resultados nem declare melhoria apenas porque o teste passou. Se o runtime independente ou a instrumentação não estiverem disponíveis, registre o bloqueio específico.

Salve um relatório de PASS/FAIL/BLOQUEADO em `workstation/benchmarks/system1_live_session/`, preserve todas as alterações existentes e não faça commit, push ou merge.

6|"""

9|from dataclasses import dataclass
10|import os
11|import re
12|import unicodedata
13|from typing import Any, Callable, Mapping

16|from workstation.system1.calibration import default_calibration_policy
17|from workstation.system1.schemas import build_candidate_ranking_schema
18|
19|_FIND = re.compile(
20|    r"^\s*(?:localize|encontre)\s+(?:o|a)\s+"
21|    r"(bot[aã]o|aba|link)\s+(.+?)\s+na\s+p[aá]gina\s+atual[.!]?\s*$",
22|    re.IGNORECASE,
23|)
24|_REFS = re.compile(r"^@e[1-9]\d*$")
25|_KINDS = {"botão": "button", "botao": "button", "aba": "tab", "link": "link"}
26|_NEUTRALS = {"NO_MATCH", "ABSTAIN"}
27|
28|
29|@dataclass(frozen=True)
30|class BrowserLocateReceipt:
31|    status: str  # verified | fallback
32|    ref: str = ""
33|    reason: str = ""
34|    provider: str = ""
35|
36|
37|def parse_find_request(text: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
38|    """Recognize a narrow explicit human read. Never interpret click/send intents."""
39|    if not isinstance(text, str) or len(text) > 180 or "\n" in text:
40|        return None
41|    match = _FIND.fullmatch(text)
42|    if not match:
43|        return None
44|    label = match.group(2).strip()
45|    if not 2 <= len(label) <= 80:
46|        return None
47|    return _KINDS[match.group(1).lower()], label
48|
49|
50|def _normalized(text: str) -> str:
51|    return "".join(
52|        c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.casefold())
53|        if not unicodedata.combining(c)
54|    ).strip()
55|
56|
57|def _eligible(snapshot: Any) -> bool:
58|    return (
59|        isinstance(snapshot, dict)
60|        and snapshot.get("success") is True
61|        and snapshot.get("runtime") == "electron-chromium"
62|        and isinstance(snapshot.get("url"), str) and bool(snapshot["url"])
63|        and isinstance(snapshot.get("task_id"), str) and bool(snapshot["task_id"])
64|        and isinstance(snapshot.get("tab_id"), str) and bool(snapshot["tab_id"])
65|        and type(snapshot.get("revision")) is int and snapshot["revision"] >= 0
66|        and snapshot.get("readiness") == "stable"
67|        and snapshot.get("truncated") is False
68|        and snapshot.get("wall_detected") is False
69|        and isinstance(snapshot.get("elements"), list)
70|        and bool(snapshot["elements"])
71|    )
72|

74|def _candidates(snapshot: Mapping[str, Any], kind: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
75|    result: list[dict[str, str]] = []
76|    seen: set[str] = set()
77|    for element in snapshot["elements"]:
78|        if not isinstance(element, dict) or element.get("disabled") is not False:
79|            continue
80|        ref = element.get("ref")
81|        role = str(element.get("role") or "").casefold()
82|        tag = str(element.get("tag") or "").casefold()
83|        label = element.get("label")
84|        if not isinstance(ref, str) or not _REFS.fullmatch(ref) or ref in seen:
85|            continue
86|        if not isinstance(label, str) or not label.strip():
87|            continue
88|        if kind == "button" and role != "button" and tag != "button":
89|            continue
90|        if kind == "link" and role != "link" and tag != "a":
91|            continue
92|        if kind == "tab" and role != "tab":
93|            continue
94|        seen.add(ref)
95|        result.append({"ref": ref, "role": role, "label": label.strip()[:80]})
96|    return result
97|
98|
99|def _same_snapshot(before: dict, after: Any, selected: dict, kind: str) -> bool:
100|    if not _eligible(after):
101|        return False
102|    if any(before[key] != after[key] for key in ("task_id", "tab_id", "revision", "url")):

104|    return any(row == selected for row in _candidates(after, kind))

107|def find_visible_control(
108|    snapshot: dict[str, Any],
109|    intent: tuple[str, str],
110|    fresh_snapshot: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]],
111|    *,

# apps/desktop/src/ — backend contract, slash palette, Bot Mode

Applies on top of `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md` (the judgment guide) and the root `AGENTS.md`.
Root TypeScript style rules apply.

## The desktop is its own chat surface on a `hermes serve` backend

Electron + React + nanostores (`@assistant-ui/react`) talking to a `tui_gateway` backend over
JSON-RPC (`requestGateway(method, params)`); transport lives in the framework-agnostic `apps/shared`
(`@hermes/shared`: `JsonRpcGatewayClient` + WS URL helpers), which the web dashboard also consumes.
The desktop has **no build/runtime dependency on the dashboard frontend**: it spawns a headless
`hermes serve` (`headless_backend=True` → `cmd_dashboard` skips `_build_web_ui` and exports
`HERMES_SERVE_HEADLESS=1` so `mount_spa()` disables the SPA even if a stray `web_dist/` exists).
`dashboard` and `serve` share `cmd_dashboard`/`start_server` but neither launches the other. It does
NOT embed `hermes --tui` — own composer, transcript, slash pipeline.

**One backward-compat fallback:** `serve` is newer, so the spawn (`electron/backend-command.ts` +
`createBackendServeSupportResolver()` in `electron/backend-serve-support.ts`) checks whether the runtime registers `serve`
and ONLY when it does not (older managed install / PATH `hermes` not yet updated) rewrites argv to
legacy `dashboard --no-open`. Without it a new app against an un-upgraded runtime crashes on an
unknown subcommand and bricks every mid-upgrade user. Keep it narrow and tested.

Lifecycle: `serve` dies with the app by design; the messaging gateway survives it (spawned detached
via `/api/gateway/*`). Never re-parent the gateway under the backend — `gateway/AGENTS.md`.

The backend the app spawns is a **pooled `hermes serve --port 0` per (connection, profile)**: its
launch home is that profile, `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` is set, and its in-process cron ticker stands down
for homes a running gateway already serves. One process may still host sessions from several homes
(`tui_gateway/AGENTS.md` § Profile scope); the first non-launch home flips `set_multiplex_active`.
Remote connections (SSH, URL+token, Cloud) reach a backend with no desktop env var that may serve
several profiles from one process. Every lifecycle/status/settings REST call against a pooled
backend carries `?profile=` (or the `profile` param) and every new-session tile records an owner
route; a backend-side scope fix is probed twice — with the profile as the launch home of a pooled
backend (env-bound) and as a secondary served by one process (override-bound).

## Slash commands: curated client-side, dispatched to the backend

- The backend already provides everything: `commands.catalog` and `complete.slash` include built-ins,
  user `quick_commands`, AND skill-derived commands. No new RPC is needed to see skills.
- `src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.ts` is the load-bearing file: `DESKTOP_COMMAND_SPECS` (built-ins
  and their desktop surfaces) + the block-list. A command's desktop disposition (terminal-only /
  messaging-only / settings-owned / advanced / hidden) is authored ONCE, as `desktop=` on its
  `CommandDef` in `hermes_cli/commands.py`; the live `commands.catalog` carries it, and
  `src/lib/desktop-slash-registry.json` (regenerate with `scripts/dump_desktop_slash_registry.py`;
  `tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_slash_registry.py` + the vitest file fail on drift) is the offline
  fallback. Only names the Python registry has never heard of (`/density`, `/details`, `/logs`,
  `/mouse` — Ink-local; `/pets`) live in `TS_ONLY_NO_DESKTOP_SURFACE`. `isDesktopSlashCommand(name)`
  gates **execution** (true
  for built-ins AND any non-built-in so typed skill/quick commands run);
  `isDesktopSlashSuggestion(name)` gates **discovery** — used by BOTH completion paths in
  `app/chat/composer/hooks/use-slash-completions.ts` and by `filterDesktopCommandsCatalog`;
  `isDesktopSlashExtensionCommand(name)` is true for anything not a known built-in, and both
  suggestion and catalog paths let extensions through (the allow-list once silently dropped every
  skill/quick command from completions even though they executed when typed).
- Dispatch: `app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/slash.ts` (`runSlash`) — desktop-owned built-ins
  (`/skin`, `/help`, `/new`, ...) locally or via `commands.catalog`; everything else `slash.exec` →
  `command.dispatch` fallback; a skill command resolves to `{type: "skill", message}` and is
  submitted as a normal prompt.

**Rule:** palette curation hides noise (terminal-only / messaging-only built-ins), NEVER
user-activated extensions. If you tighten `desktop-slash-commands.ts`, keep
`isDesktopSlashExtensionCommand` flowing into both paths. Test: from `apps/desktop`,
`npx vitest run src/lib/desktop-slash-commands.test.ts` (workspace deps install at the repo root).

## Bot Mode (`src/plugins/hermes-bots/`) — one bot = ONE canonical forever-chat, identified by NAME

Each bot is a Hermes **profile** with a persistent identity. This invariant regressed repeatedly,
cost users conversation history each time, and is not open for re-litigation in a routine PR.

The chat's only identity is **(profile, session titled exactly "Bot Chat")**; the state DB's
UNIQUE(title) index makes that pair a registry of at most one row. Clicking a bot row:
1. **Resolve the registry, every time:** `session.list {title, include_hidden: true}` (indexed,
   window-free; hidden rows resolve because canonical chats are always hidden; compression lineages
   resolve to the live tip). Row exists → open it. That is the whole happy path.
2. **No row → create it**, titled `Bot Chat`, born hidden, kicked off with the bot's intro. Creation
   adopts-before-minting: it re-runs the lookup first so a concurrent/pre-existing row is opened,
   never forked (`set_session_title` silently drops conflicting titles — returns 0 rows — which is how
   the 2026-08 infinite fork loop started).

**There is NO session-id pin.** The old design stored a pointer in `ui_meta['hermes-bots'].chat`;
five hardening waves (#88690, #90732, #90751, the #91791 revert, #92042) each guarded a new way it
dangled or was stolen (rows[0] steals, `last_session` adoptions, transient clears, a pin re-anchored
onto a cron session). A name cannot dangle; legacy `chat` keys in ui_meta are ignored and dropped.
**Recency must never win** (#91791 → #92042): canonical Bot Chats are unconditionally hidden from the
Sessions sidebar, so the bot row is the ONLY door — "newest visible session wins" walls the whole
relationship off behind a row that previews one session and opens another. Side-chats ("New chat
with this agent") are not plumbing-titled, stay visible in the sidebar, and are never the row's target.

Reviewer corollaries: no per-bot session browser (removed in #90732; don't add it back). Reject any
stored session-id pointer as canonical identity — including "as a fallback tier" or "for
verification". Reject anything consulting recency/visibility/"where the user left off" for the row's
target; such reports are about side-chats and the fix belongs in the Sessions sidebar hide-sweep.
The gateway reports the registry row as `canonical_session` on `profiles.list` (resolved server-side
by title); roster preview, activity signals, and the `/new`→`/compact` guard all read it, so preview
identity and click identity are the same row by construction. Contract tests:

{"output": "# Hermes Work — Qualificação System 1 Browser + Laya (07/11/2026)

**Decisão:** rota de produção não promovida; permanece **desabilitada por padrão** (`HERMES_SYSTEM1_BROWSER_FASTPATH_ENABLED` diferente de `1`). Critérios pendentes: mensagem humana real no Desktop → TaskRun autenticado → recibo verificado → comparação real de chamadas/custo do System 2. Provas isoladas não substituem esse gate.

## Ambiente e preservação
- Checkout compartilhado: `C:\Github\hermes-agent`, `main@f1d5ab2f03`. Havia **358 entradas modificadas/não rastreadas** no preflight, de diversas missões. Não houve reset, stash, clean, switch, commit, push, merge ou reinício do Hermes.
- Processo Hermes ativo usa `C:\Github\hermes-agent\.venv`; Laya continua ausente desse ambiente.
- PM criou somente **dois ambientes laterais** em `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HermesWorkstation\qualification\system1-laya` (requisitos mínimos para benchmark) e `...\system1-laya-project` (dependências fechadas do Hermes + extra `system1-laya`). Nenhum foi selecionado como ambiente do aplicativo ativo.
- Proveniência estrita no ambiente PM: **PASS**, Laya `0.3.23`, Torch `2.14.1+cpu`, Transformers `5.18.0`; bytes da fonte vendorizada e origem do pacote confirmados. Modelo multilíngue em cache local; inferências realizadas com `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` e `TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1`.

## Prova de inferência em português (CPU, 9 casos)
Evidência: `workstation/benchmarks/system1_laya_pt_results_20261107.json`, produzido por `workstation/benchmarks/system1_laya_pt_qualification.py`.
- Primeira passagem **antes do hard guard**: 7/9 corretos, 1 falso aceite. Duplicidade: o Laya escolheu um de dois botões idênticos “Relatórios”, confiança 0,9012. Risco inaceitável.
- TDD: dois testes RED reais (`test_duplicate_exact_labels_fail_closed_before_model`, `test_two_partial_matches_fail_closed_before_model`), depois GREEN. O guard passou a rejeitar ambiguidades **antes da inferência**, preservando fallback e sem afetar os executores.
- Reexecução guardada: **8/9 corretos, 0 falsos aceites, 4 fallbacks**, p50 de inferência aquecida **272,38ms** e máxima aquecida **310,45ms**. A primeira inferência levou **10,15s** com carregamento. O caso “Calendário editorial” foi respondido corretamente pelo modelo, mas abstido pelo limiar de confiança (0,4119); não mascarar esse caso.
- Esses casos são sintéticos. N=9 não demonstra robustez geral e a latência do modelo não prova economia frente ao System 2.

## Provas integradas
- `workstation/benchmarks/system1_laya_hermes_smoke.py` executado no ambiente de projeto PM: provedor real `LayaDecisionProvider`, pergunta parcial em português, modelo correto, ref `@e1` verificada e **DecisionReceipt** persistido em diretório sandbox.
- `node apps/desktop/e2e/workstation-system1-native-snapshot-runner.cjs`, passando `HERMES_LAYA_QUAL_PYTHON` apontando para o Python isolado: **PASS / exit 0**. Criou Chromium Electron isolado com fixture local 127.0.0.1, capturou 9 snapshots reais e passou dois deles ao provedor Laya real; modelo selecionou `@e1` para “Relatório” com confiança **0,9811**, readback independente validou a mesma referência e confirmou receipt.

- `scripts/run_tests.sh workstation/tests/test_system1_browser_read_fastpath.py workstation/tests/test_operational_resolution_provider.py workstation/tests/prefabs/test_prefabs.py workstation/tests/test_system1_capability_routing.py workstation/tests/test_system1_safety.py -j 3 -q`: **59 PASS, 0 FAIL** (suites focadas, não a suíte total).
- `ruff check` nos arquivos Python modificados/adicionados: **PASS**; `git diff --check` no arquivo versionado alterado: **PASS**.
- Teste RED→GREEN da configuração: sem flag, `maybe_resolve_browser_find` tentava construir dispatcher; agora retorna `None` antes de qualquer IO e o caminho anterior permanece inalterado. Teste de habilitação explícita usa flag **somente dentro do processo de teste**.

1. **Fluxo realmente originado na UI humana do Desktop** com TaskRun/BrowserTask de teste e identidade coerente: não foi executado. É proibido enviar um prompt/abrir uma nova tarefa na sessão produtiva ou alterar o ledger dela para suprir essa lacuna. Um teste com envelope humano mockado ou snapshot real isolado **não equivale** a essa prova.

Se houver necessidade de promoção, montar uma **sessão de teste verdadeiramente isolada** (UI + backend + BrowserTask + armazenamento + provedor de modelo), enviar uma mensagem humana de localização read-only via ponte autorizada, registrar chamadas System 2, latência p50/p95 e readback, comparar com a mesma tarefa pelo caminho antigo e só então decidir ativar a rota. **Não tocar nas sessões, filas, leases ou ledgers produtivos.**

{"content": """"Component-level live-input bench for the System 1 browser read fast path.

Inputs are REAL native snapshots captured from this desktop session's BrowserTask
(live_snapshots_20261107.json). The bench exercises workstation.system1.
browser_read_fastpath.find_visible_control with the real LayaDecisionProvider
loaded from the isolated PM environment.

It is NOT an end-to-end human-origin homologation run: the fast path entry point
(maybe_resolve_browser_find) is gated by HERMES_SYSTEM1_BROWSER_FASTPATH_ENABLED
and executes only inside an agent turn. This script never touches that gate, never
dispatches a browser operation and never clicks anything.

Run:
    <isolated-pm-python> workstation/benchmarks/system1_live_session/run_component_bench_20261107.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import platform
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

FIXTURE = Path(__file__).with_name("live_snapshots_20261107.json")


def main() -> int:
    from workstation.system1.browser_read_fastpath import find_visible_control
    from workstation.system1.laya_provider import LayaDecisionProvider

    provider = LayaDecisionProvider()
    try:
        provider._ensure_router()
        provider_state = "loaded"
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - availability probe
        provider_state = f"unavailable: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"

    calls: list[dict] = []

    def counting_decide(request):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        result = provider.decide(request)
        calls.append(
            {
                "ms": round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2),
                "provider": getattr(result, "provider", None),
                "answers": dict(getattr(result, "answers", {}) or {}),
                "confidence": dict(getattr(result, "confidence", {}) or {}),
                "abstentions": list(getattr(result, "abstentions", []) or []),
                "fallback_recommended": getattr(result, "fallback_recommended", None),
            }
        )
        return result

    fixture = json.loads(FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    results = {}
    for name, scenario in fixture["scenarios"].items():
        calls.clear()
        readbacks = {"count": 0}

        def readback(before=scenario["before"], after=scenario["after"]):
            readbacks["count"] += 1
            return after

        started = time.perf_counter()
        receipt = find_visible_control(
            dict(scenario["before"]),
            tuple(scenario["intent"]),
            readback,
            decide=counting_decide,
        )
        elapsed = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
        results[name] = {
            "url": scenario["url"],
            "intent": scenario["intent"],
            "status": receipt.status,
            "ref": receipt.ref,
            "reason": receipt.reason,
            "provider": receipt.provider,
            "total_ms": elapsed,
            "readback_calls": readbacks["count"],
            "system1_calls": len(calls),
            "system1_call_ms": [c["ms"] for c in calls],
            "system1_detail": calls[:3],
            "navigate_operation_id": scenario["navigate_receipt"]["operationId"],
            "navigate_revision": scenario["navigate_receipt"]["revision"],
        }

    report = {
        "schema": "hermes.system1.live_session.component_bench.v1",
        "kind": "component-level (NOT an end-to-end human-origin turn)",
        "ran_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "python": sys.version.split()[0],
        "executable": sys.executable,
        "platform": platform.platform(),
        "fastpath_env": os.environ.get("HERMES_SYSTEM1_BROWSER_FASTPATH_ENABLED"),
        "provider": provider_state,
        "laya_version": getattr(provider.provenance, "laya_version", None),
        "laya_source_sha": getattr(provider.provenance, "laya_source_sha", None),
        "model": getattr(provider.provenance, "model", None),
        "device": getattr(provider.provenance, "device", None),
        "calibration_id": getattr(provider.provenance, "calibration_id", None),
        "results": results,
    }
    out = Path(__file__).with_name("component_bench_20261107.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    print(f"\nwritten: {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

{"content": """"Collect real backend/turn evidence for the System 1 live session.

Read-only: reads the running backend's interpreter probe, the kanban task record
and the workstation telemetry ledger. Writes a JSON evidence file next to this
script. Never mutates sessions, leases, ledgers or browser state.

Run with the LIVE backend interpreter (.venv) so the laya probe reflects the
backend that actually serves the human messages:

    C:\\Github\\hermes-agent\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe \
        workstation/benchmarks/system1_live_session/collect_turn_evidence_20261107.py --since <iso8601>
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SESSION_ID = "20261107_175035_62899b"
TASK_ID = "t_1863c0f1"


def hermes_home() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("HERMES_HOME") or Path.home() / ".hermes")


def laya_probe() -> dict:
    spec = importlib.util.find_spec("laya")
    version = None
    if spec is not None:
        try:
            import laya  # noqa: PLC0415

            version = getattr(laya, "__version__", None)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
            version = f"import_error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    return {
        "interpreter": sys.executable,
        "python": sys.version.split()[0],
        "laya_importable": spec is not None,
        "laya_version": version,
    }


def provider_registration_probe() -> dict:
    """Ask the backend interpreter which system1 provider, if any, registers."""
    code = (
        "import json\n"
        "try:\n"
        "    from agent.system1_decision import decide_system1\n"
        "    import agent.system1_decision as m\n"
        "    p = getattr(m, '_PROVIDER', None)\n"
        "    print(json.dumps({'registered': p is not None, 'provider': type(p).__name__ if p else None}))\n"
        "except Exception as exc:\n"
        "    print(json.dumps({'registered': False, 'error': f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}'}))\n"
    )
    out = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=str(REPO), timeout=180
    )
    tail = (out.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["{}"]
    try:
        return json.loads(tail[0])
    except ValueError:
        return {"registered": None, "raw": tail[0][:200], "stderr": (out.stderr or "")[-200:]}


def kanban_task() -> dict:
    path = hermes_home() / "kanban.db"
    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    row = con.execute(
        "select id,title,status,session_id,current_run_id,created_by,completion_contract,created_at "
        "from tasks where id=?",
        (TASK_ID,),
    ).fetchone()
    return dict(row) if row else {}


def telemetry(since: str | None) -> dict:
    path = hermes_home() / "workstation" / "telemetry" / "telemetry.sqlite"
    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    where = "session_id=?" + (" and occured_at>=?" if False else "")
    params: list = [SESSION_ID]
    sql = (
        "select event_type,count(*) n,coalesce(sum(provider_calls),0) provider_calls,"
        "coalesce(sum(tool_calls),0) tool_calls,coalesce(sum(input_tokens),0) input_tokens,"
        "coalesce(sum(output_tokens),0) output_tokens,coalesce(sum(duration_ms),0) duration_ms "
        "from events where session_id=?"
    )
    if since:
        sql += " and occurred_at>=?"
        params.append(since)
    sql += " group by event_type order by n desc"
    groups = [dict(r) for r in con.execute(sql, params)]
    system1 = [
        dict(r)
        for r in con.execute(
            "select occurred_at,status,provider_calls,duration_ms,payload_json from events "
            "where event_type='SYSTEM1_COMPLETED' and session_id=? order by occurred_at desc limit 5",
            (SESSION_ID,),
        )
    ]
    provider_calls = [
        dict(r)
        for r in con.execute(
            "select occurred_at,turn_id,call_id,provider_calls,duration_ms,input_tokens,output_tokens,status "
            "from events where event_type='PROVIDER_CALLED' and session_id=?"
            + (" and occurred_at>=?" if since else "")
            + " order by occurred_at",
            [SESSION_ID] + ([since] if since else []),
        )
    ]
    browser_ops = [
        dict(r)
        for r in con.execute(
            "select occurred_at,operation_id,status,duration_ms,route,payload_json from events "
            "where event_type='BROWSER_OPERATION_OBSERVED' and session_id=?"
            + (" and occurred_at>=?" if since else "")
            + " order by occurred_at",
            [SESSION_ID] + ([since] if since else []),
        )
    ]
    return {
        "window_since": since,
        "event_groups": groups,
        "system1_completed": system1,
        "provider_calls": provider_calls,
        "browser_operations": browser_ops,
    }


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--since", default=None, help="ISO8601 UTC lower bound for the turn window")
    ap.add_argument("--note", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    evidence = {
        "schema": "hermes.system1.live_session.evidence.v1",
        "collected_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "session_id": SESSION_ID,
        "task_id": TASK_ID,
        "fastpath_flag": os.environ.get("HERMES_SYSTEM1_BROWSER_FASTPATH_ENABLED"),
        "hermes_python_env": os.environ.get("HERMES_PYTHON"),
        "backend_interpreter_probe": laya_probe(),
        "provider_registration": provider_registration_probe(),
        "kanban_task": kanban_task(),
        "telemetry": telemetry(args.since),
        "note": args.note,
    }
    out = Path(__file__).with_name("evidence_preflight_20261107.json" if not args.since else "evidence_turn_20261107.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(evidence, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    summary = {
        "flag": evidence["fastpath_flag"],
        "laya_importable": evidence["backend_interpreter_probe"]["laya_importable"],
        "provider_registration": evidence["provider_registration"],
        "task": {k: evidence["kanban_task"].get(k) for k in ("id", "status", "session_id", "current_run_id")},
        "provider_calls": len(evidence["telemetry"]["provider_calls"]),
        "tool_events": {g["event_type"]: g["n"] for g in evidence["telemetry"]["event_groups"]},
        "system1_completed": len(evidence["telemetry"]["system1_completed"]),
    }
    print(json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    print(f"written: {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
